Al-Farra' said: "We have held them back from spending in the way of God." Abu 'Ubayda said: "We have prevented them from faith by means of barriers." Since the *ghull* (shackle or iron collar) prevents the one who is shackled from moving and turning, the *ghull* upon the heart prevents faith.

If it is asked: the shackle that prevents faith is the one in the heart, so why does He mention the shackle around the neck?

It is answered: since it is the custom for a shackle to be placed on the neck, He mentioned its place, and what is meant by it is the heart. As in His saying, ﴿And every person's omen We have fastened to his neck﴾.

From this is the saying of people, "Let it be on your neck," and "This is on your neck."

From this is His saying, ﴿And do not make your hand chained to your neck﴾.

He likened withholding from spending to the hand when it is chained to the neck.

From this, al-Farra' said regarding ﴿Indeed, We have put shackles around their necks﴾: "We have held them back from spending."

Abu Ishaq said: "The expression 'this is on the neck of so-and-so' is used of a thing that is binding, meaning its binding is like the binding of a necklace, among the things worn on the neck." Abu 'Ali said: "This is like their saying, 'I have put on you such-and-such, and I have made you wear it as a necklace (qalada).'" From it is the saying, "The sultan entrusted (qallada) him with such-and-such," meaning the authority became binding upon him in the place of the necklace and the collar.

I say: From this is the saying, "I entrusted (qalladtu) so-and-so with the ruling of such-and-such," as if you made it a collar on his neck.

God has named burdensome obligations "shackles" in His saying, ﴿He relieves them of their burden and the shackles that were upon them﴾.

So He likened them to shackles because of their severity and difficulty. Al-Hasan said: "They are the hardships that existed in worship, such as cutting off the traces of urine and impurity, killing oneself in repentance, cutting off the sinful limbs, and removing the veins from the flesh."

Ibn Qutayba said: "They are the many things God, glorified is He, forbade them, which He had permitted for the community of Muhammad (ﷺ), and He made them shackles because prohibition restrains, just as a shackle restrains the hand."

As for His saying, ﴿So they are up to the chins﴾, a group said: the pronoun refers to the hands, even though they were not mentioned, because the context indicates them. They said: because the shackle is around the neck, the hand is brought together to it, and for this reason it is called a *jami'a* (a binding that gathers). On this view the meaning is: "their hands, or their right hands, are gathered up to their chins." This is the view of al-Farra' and al-Zajjaj.

Another group said: the pronoun refers to the shackles. This is the apparent meaning.

His saying, ﴿So they are up to the chins﴾, means: connected and fastened to them. It is a wide shackle that has encircled the neck until it reaches the chin.

His saying, ﴿So they are raised-up (muqmahun)﴾.

Al-Farra' and al-Zajjaj said: *al-muqmah* is one whose gaze is lowered after raising his head.

The meaning of *al-iqmah* in the language is raising the head and lowering the gaze. It is said: "The camel raised (aqmaha) its head, and it was raised (qamaha)."

Al-Asma'i said: "A camel is *qami'* when it raises its head from the watering trough and does not drink."

Al-Azhari said: "When their hands were chained to their necks, the shackles raised their chins and heads upward, like camels raising their heads." End of quotation.

If it is asked: what is the point of comparison between this and the restraint of the heart from guidance and faith?

It is answered: it is the best and clearest aspect. When the shackle is on the neck and the hands are gathered to it, it prevents the hand from acting and seizing. When it is wide, filling the neck and reaching the chin, it prevents the head from lowering. It makes its wearer's head fixed and upright, and he cannot move it. Then His saying confirms this meaning of restraint: ﴿And We have put before them a barrier and behind them a barrier, and covered them, so they do not see﴾.

Ibn ʿAbbas said: "He prevented them from guidance because of what had already passed in His knowledge, and the barrier (sadd) placed before them and behind them is what blocked the path of guidance for them." So He informed, glorified be He, of the obstacles by which He prevented them from faith, as a punishment for them, and He illustrated them with the best and most eloquent illustration, namely the condition of a day when wide collars reaching up to the chins were placed upon their necks, their hands were drawn up to them, and they were made to stand between two barriers, unable to pass through between them, and their sight was covered so that they see nothing.

If you reflect upon the condition of the disbeliever who recognised the truth and it became clear to him, then rejected it, denied it, and opposed it with the utmost opposition, you will find that this illustration corresponds to his state with the most complete correspondence, and that a barrier has been placed between him and faith just as it has been placed between these people and free action. And Allah is the One whose help is sought.

Ibn al-Qayyim combined the two books: the earlier book that records their deeds before they exist, and the book that accompanies their deeds. He thus informed that He revives them after they have died, for resurrection, and recompenses them for their deeds. By His writing of them he drew attention to this. He said, ﴿We write down what they have sent forward﴾, whether good or evil that they did in their lifetime, and "their traces," meaning what they established of a good or evil practice, so that others follow them in it after their death.

Ibn 'Abbas, in the narration of 'Ata', said: "Their traces" means what they left behind of good or evil, like His saying: ﴿Man will be informed on that Day of what he sent forward and left behind﴾.

If you say: this has already been derived from His saying ﴿what they have sent forward﴾, so what does His saying ﴿their traces﴾ add to it?

I say: it adds a great benefit, namely that He, glorified is He, writes what they did and what arises from their deeds. Thus what arises from them is as though they did it, whether good or evil, and it is the trace of their deeds. So "their traces" are the traces of their deeds that arise from them.

This view is more general than the view of Muqatil. It seems that Muqatil intended an example and an illustration, following the habit of the early scholars (al-salaf) of explaining a general term by a type or an individual instance of its meaning, as an approximation and illustration, not as a restriction or comprehensive enumeration.

Anas and Ibn 'Abbas, in the narration of 'Ikrimah, said: "This verse was revealed concerning the Banu Salamah. They wished to move closer to the mosque, for their dwellings were far away. When it was revealed, they said: 'Rather, we shall remain where we are.'"

The proponents of this view relied on what is in Sahih al-Bukhari from the hadith of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, who said:

"The Banu Salamah were in a part of Madinah, and they wished to move to near the mosque, so this verse was revealed: ﴿Indeed, it is We who bring the dead to life, and We write down what they have sent forward and their traces﴾.

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'O Banu Salamah, stay in your homes; your traces are being written.'"

Muslim also narrated something similar in his Sahih from the hadith of Jabir and Anas. However, this view requires examination, for Surah Ya-Sin is Meccan, while the story of the Banu Salamah took place in Madinah, unless it is said that this verse alone is Madani.

Better than this is that it was mentioned at the occasion of this story and pointed to it, and they were reminded of it there, either by the Prophet (ﷺ) or by Jibril, and so this was called "revelation" (nuzul). 

Perhaps this is what those who say in similar cases "it was revealed twice" intended.

The point is that their steps to the mosques are among their traces which Allah writes for them.

'Umar ibn al-Khattab said: "If Allah, glorified is He, were leaving anything of the son of Adam, He would leave what the wind has effaced of his traces."

Masruq said: "No man takes a step except that a good or evil deed is written for him."

The point is that His saying ﴿And everything We have enumerated in a clear Imam﴾, which is the Preserved Tablet, the Mother of the Book, the Reminder in which everything is recorded, includes the writing of the deeds of the servants before they perform them.

The enumeration in the Book includes His knowledge of them, His preservation of them, His encompassing of their number, and their establishment within it.

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 36, verses 20–22:

He drew attention to what makes following obligatory, which is that the one followed is a messenger, to whom one should not oppose or disobey, and that he is upon guidance. He also drew attention to the absence of any impediment, which is that he does not ask for a reward; so he does not seek from you worldly gain or leadership. Therefore, what makes following obligatory is that he is guided, and the impediment to it is absent, namely the seeking of exaltation on earth, corruption, and the seeking of a reward.

Then he said: ﴿And why should I not worship He who originated me?﴾ [Ya-Sin: 22]

He presented the proof against them in the form of addressing himself, as a means of winning them over. He drew attention to the fact that worshipping the servant of the One who originated him is a matter required by the intellects, and abandoning it is abhorrent; neglecting it is a grave wrong. For His creating His servant is the root of His bestowing favour upon him, and every other blessing follows from His bringing him into existence and creating him. Allah has innately disposed intellects and natures to thank the benefactor and to love the one who does good. One should not give heed to what the deniers of the rational goodness and badness (of acts) (nufat al-tahsin wa al-taqbih) say on this matter, for it is among the most corrupt and invalid of statements in intellects, natures and laws.

Then he turned to them, warning them as a sincere advisor warns, and said: ﴿And to Him you will be returned.﴾

Then he informed them about the deities that are worshipped besides Him, that they are false and that worshipping them is false, and he said: ﴿Shall I take besides Him gods, if the Most Merciful intends for me some harm, their intercession will not avail me at all, nor can they save me?﴾ [Ya-Sin: 23]

For the worshipper wants from his worshipped one that it benefit him at the time of his need. Indeed, if the Most Merciful, who originated me, intends for me harm, these deities would have no power to rescue me from that harm, nor any standing or position with Him by which they could intercede for me to free me from that harm. So in what way would they deserve worship?

And ﴿Indeed, I would then be in manifest error﴾ if I worshipped besides Allah what has this condition.

(Benefit)

This is what Allah, glorified and exalted be He, related about the companion of Ya-Sin, in a manner of approval of this statement, praise of the one who said it, and affirmation of it. None of the Companions asked us for a reward, and they are guided, by the proof of His saying, addressing them: ﴿And you were on the brink of a pit of the Fire, and He saved you from it. Thus does Allah make clear to you His signs, that you may be guided.﴾ [Al 'Imran: 103]

And "la'alla" (perhaps/that you may) from Allah is binding. And His saying: ﴿And among them are those who listen to you, until when they leave your presence they say to those who were given knowledge, "What did he just say?" Those are the ones upon whose hearts Allah has set a seal, and who follow their desires.﴾ [Muhammad: 16]

﴿And those who are guided, He increases them in guidance and gives them their piety.﴾ [Muhammad: 17]

And His saying: ﴿And those who are killed in the way of Allah, He will not let their deeds be lost. He will guide them.﴾ [Muhammad: 4–5]

And His saying: ﴿And those who strive for Us, We will surely guide them to Our paths.﴾ [Al-'Ankabut: 69]

Each of them fought in the way of Allah and strove, either with his hand or with his tongue. So Allah has guided them, and whoever Allah has guided is guided, and so it is obligatory to follow him, by the verse.

**Section: On the mention of the marriage of the people of Paradise, their intercourse with their spouses, and their enjoyment of it in the most perfect pleasure and purity, free from madhy (pre-seminal fluid) and maniy (seminal fluid), weakness, and the fact that it does not require ghusl (ritual bath).**

The hadith of Abu Hurayrah has already been mentioned. It was said: "O Messenger of Allah ﷺ, shall we have intercourse with our wives in Paradise?" He said: "Indeed, a man will have intercourse with a hundred virgins in a single day."

Its chain of narration is sound.

The hadith of Abu Musa, whose authenticity is agreed upon (Muttafaq 'alayh), has already been mentioned: "Indeed, the believer in Paradise has a tent of a single hollow pearl, sixty miles long, and in it are his family, whom he goes around to visit."

And the hadith of Anas: "The believer in Paradise is given the strength of so-and-so many men."

al-Tirmidhi authenticated it.

al-Tabarani, Abd Allah ibn Ahmad, and others narrated from the hadith of Laqit ibn Amir that he said: "O Messenger of Allah ﷺ, what is in what comes forth from Paradise?" He said: "Rivers of purified honey, rivers of wine with no headache or intoxication in it, rivers of milk whose taste does not change, water that does not stagnate, fruits of the kind you know, and better than that, and purified spouses." I said: "O Messenger of Allah ﷺ, will there be for us in it righteous spouses?" He said: "The righteous women are for the righteous men. Enjoy them with your pleasure of this world, but with the enjoyment being without procreation."

Ibn Wahb said: Amr ibn al-Harith informed me, from Daraj, from Abu Hujayrah, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Messenger of Allah, that he said: "O Messenger of Allah ﷺ, will we have intercourse in Paradise?" He said: "Yes, by the One in whose hand is my soul, dahman dahman (vigorously). Then when he rises from her, she returns purified and a virgin."

al-Tabarani said: Ibrahim ibn Jabir al-Faqih narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Malik al-Duqayqi al-Wasiti, from Ya'la ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Wasiti, from Shurayk, from Asim al-Ahwal, from Abu al-Mutawakkil, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Indeed, when the people of Paradise have intercourse with their wives, they return as virgins."

al-Tabarani said: No one narrated this from Asim except Shurayk, and he was alone in it, having narrated it from Ya'la.

al-Tabarani said: Abdan ibn Ahmad narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahim al-Barqi, from Amr ibn Abi Salamah, from Sadaqah, from Hashim ibn Zayd, from Sulaym ibn Abi Yahya, that he heard Abu Umamah relate that he heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he was asked: "Do the people of Paradise marry?" He said: "With a male member that never tires, and a desire that never ends, dahman dahman."

al-Tabarani said: Ahmad ibn Yahya al-Hulwani narrated to us, from Suwayd ibn Sa'id, from Khalid ibn Yazid ibn Abi Malik, from his father, from Khalid ibn Ma'dan, from Abu Umamah, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was asked: "Do the people of Paradise have intercourse?" He said: "Dahan dahan (vigorously), but there is no maniy and no mniyah (death)."

Hashim and Khalid, although they have been spoken of, are not relied upon.

As for his saying "la mana wa la mniyah" (no maniy and no mniyah): that means no emission and no death.

Abu Nu'aym said: Abu Ali Muhammad ibn Ahmad narrated to us, from Bishr ibn Musa, from Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Muqri', from Abd al-Rahman ibn Ziyad, from Umarah ibn Rashid, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, that he was asked: "Do the people of Paradise touch their spouses?" He said: "Yes, by the One who sent me with the truth: a male member that never tires, a private part that never fails, and a desire that never ends."

al-Hasan ibn Sufyan said in his Musnad: Hisham ibn Ammar narrated to us, from Sadaqah ibn Khalid, from Uthman ibn Abi al-Atikah, from Ali ibn Zayd, from al-Qasim, from Abu Umamah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was asked: "Do the people of Paradise marry?" He said: "Yes, by the One who sent me with the truth, dahman dahman," and he gestured with his hand, "but there is no maniy and no mniyah."

Sa'id ibn Mansur said: Sufyan narrated to us, from Amr, from Ikrimah, concerning the words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, the companions of Paradise today are busy in joyful occupation﴾

He said: "In the deflowering of virgins."

Abd Allah ibn Ahmad said: Abu al-Rabi' al-Zahrani and Muhammad ibn Humayd narrated to us, both saying: Ya'qub ibn Abd Allah narrated to us, from Hafs ibn Humayd, from Bishr ibn Atiyyah, from Shaqiq ibn Salamah, from Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud, concerning His words: ﴿Indeed, the companions of Paradise today are busy in joyful occupation﴾

He said: "Their occupation is the deflowering of virgins."

al-Hakim said: al-Asamm informed us, from al-Abbas ibn al-Walid, who informed me, from Shu'ayb, from al-Awza'i, concerning the words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, the companions of Paradise today are busy in joyful occupation﴾

He said: "Their occupation is the deflowering of virgins." Muqatil said: "They are occupied with the deflowering of virgins, so they do not remember the people of the Fire and do not concern themselves with them."

Abu al-Ahwas said: "They are occupied with the deflowering of virgins, away from the couches in the canopies."

Sulayman al-Taymi said, from Abu Majlaz: I asked Ibn Abbas about the words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, the companions of Paradise today are busy in joyful occupation﴾. "What is their occupation?"

He said: "The deflowering of virgins."

Ibn Abi al-Dunya said: Fudayl ibn Abd al-Wahid narrated to us, from Yazid ibn Zuray', from Sulayman al-Taymi, from Abu Amr, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, concerning "busy in joyful occupation," that he said: "It is the deflowering of virgins."

Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, from Yahya ibn Yaman, from Ash'ath, from Ja'far, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr:

"Indeed, his desire flows through his body for seventy years, he finds pleasure, and no ritual impurity (janabah) befalls them that would require them to purify themselves, nor weakness nor loss of strength. Rather, their intercourse is intercourse of delight and bliss, with no defect in it in any way whatsoever."

The most perfect of people in this regard are those who most guarded themselves in this world from what is forbidden. Just as one who drank wine in this world will not drink it in the Hereafter, and one who wore silk in this world will not wear it in the Hereafter, and one who ate from vessels of gold and silver in this world will not eat from them in the Hereafter, as the Prophet ﷺ said: "They are for them in this world, and for you in the Hereafter."

So whoever uses up his good things and pleasures in this abode, he will be deprived of them there, just as the Exalted noted with disapproval toward those who squandered their good things in the world and enjoyed them. For this reason, the Companions and those who followed them feared this with the utmost fear.

Imam Ahmad mentioned from Jabir ibn Abd Allah that Umar saw him with meat he had bought for his family for a dirham, and said: "What is this?" He said: "Meat I bought for my family for a dirham." He said: "Does every one of you, whenever he desires something, buy it? Have you not heard Allah the Exalted say: ﴿You squandered your good things in your worldly life and enjoyed them﴾?"

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 36, verses 60–61:

Does someone who makes a partner between Him and His enemy in what is purely His right of reverence, glorification, obedience, humility, submission, fear and hope truly measure Him with His due measure? If He were given a partner in that from the closest of creation to Him, that would be audacity and an assault upon what is purely His right, contempt toward Him, and an association of Him with others, and it neither befits nor is suitable except for Him, glorified is He. So how much more so when the one He is associated with is the most hated of creation to Him, the most despised by Him, the most detested in His sight, and who is, in reality, His enemy? For none is worshipped besides Allah except Satan, as the Exalted said:

﴿Did I not charge you, O children of Adam, that you should not worship Satan? Indeed, he is to you a clear enemy. And that you should worship Me; this is a straight path.﴾ [Ya-Sin 36:60–61]

When the polytheists worshipped the angels, according to their claim, their worship in reality fell upon the devils, while they thought they were worshipping the angels.

As the Exalted said: ﴿And on the Day He will gather them all, then He will say to the angels, "Did these used to worship you?" They will say, "Exalted are You; You are our Protector, not them. Rather, they used to worship the jinn; most of them were believers in them."﴾ [Saba' 34:40–41]

So Satan calls the polytheist to worship himself, and makes him imagine that he is an angel. Likewise are the worshippers of the sun, the moon and the stars: these are the ones that address them and fulfil their needs. For this reason, when the sun rises, Satan accompanies it, so the disbelievers prostrate to it, and their prostration falls to him. Likewise at its setting. Likewise whoever worships the Messiah and his mother, he has not worshipped them, but has worshipped Satan.

For he claims that he worships whoever commanded him to worship him and his mother, and was pleased with that for them and commanded them to it. This is the accursed Satan, not the servant of Allah and His messenger. So all of this descends upon His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Did I not charge you, O children of Adam, that you should not worship Satan? Indeed, he is to you a clear enemy – and that you should worship Me; this is a straight path.﴾

No one among the children of Adam worships other than Allah, whoever he may be, except that his worship falls to Satan. So the worshipper enjoys the worshipped in the attainment of his aim, and the worshipped enjoys the worshipper in his glorification of him and his association with Allah, which is the utmost of Satan's pleasure. For this reason the Exalted said: ﴿And on the Day He will gather them all, "O assembly of jinn, you have taken much of mankind," – i.e., of their misguidance and leading astray – ﴿And their allies among mankind will say, "Our Lord, some of us enjoyed others, and we have reached our term which You appointed for us." He will say, "The Fire is your residence, abiding therein eternally, except what Allah wills. Indeed, your Lord is Wise and Knowing."﴾ [al-An'am 6:128]

This is a subtle indication of the secret for which shirk is the greatest of major sins with Allah, that He does not forgive it without repentance from it, that it necessitates eternal abiding in punishment, and that its prohibition and ugliness are not merely by the bare prohibition against it. Rather, it is impossible for Allah, glorified is He, to legislate for His servants the worship of a god other than Him, just as it is impossible for Him to have what contradicts the attributes of His perfection and the qualities of His majesty. And how could it be supposed of the One singled out with lordship, divinity, greatness and glory that He would permit a partner in that, or be pleased with it? Exalted is Allah above that, a supreme exaltation.

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 36, verse 78–83:

These verses contain ten proofs:

The first is His saying: ﴿Does not man see that We created him from a drop of sperm?﴾

He reminds him of the beginning of his creation so that it may lead him to the second creation. Then He informs that this denier, if he had remembered his creation, would not have coined the parable; rather, it was when he forgot his creation that he coined the parable. So in His saying ﴿and forgets his creation﴾ there is the most subtle answer and the clearest proof. Then He informs that this denier, if he had remembered his creation, would not have coined the parable; rather, it was when he forgot his creation that he coined the parable. So in His saying ﴿and forgets his creation﴾ there is the most subtle answer and the clearest proof. This is like saying to one who denies that you had given him something: "So-and-so denies my kindness to him and forgets the clothes he wears, the wealth he has, and the house he lives in, where it is not possible for him to deny that this came from you." Then his question is answered with what includes the most eloquent proof for the establishment of what he denied, so He said: ﴿Say: He will give them life who created them the first time.﴾

This is a decisive answer and argument. Then He emphasized this meaning by informing of His comprehensive knowledge of all creation. If restoration were impossible for Him, it would be only because of deficiency in His knowledge or deficiency in His power; but there is no deficiency in the knowledge of One who is ﴿All-Knowing of every creation﴾, and there is no power above the power of Him who created the heavens and the earth, and when He wills a thing He says to it "Be," and it is. ﴿In His hand is the dominion of all things.﴾ So how could His power and knowledge fall short of giving you life after your death, when We did not fall short in the first creation, nor in creating the heavens and the earth? Then He guided His servants to a clear and evident proof that includes the answer to the doubts of the deniers, in the most subtle and clearest manner and the nearest to reason, so He said: ﴿He who produces for you fire from the green tree, and then you ignite from it.﴾

Thus this is a proof of the completeness of His power and of bringing the dead out of their graves, just as He brought fire out of the green tree.

In this there is also an answer to the doubt of those who deny the Resurrection and say: death is cold and dry, while life's nature is moisture and heat; so when death settles in the body, life cannot enter it afterward, because of the opposition between them. This is a doubt fitting for the minds of the deniers who have neither hearing nor reason; for life does not coexist with death in the same place so as to necessitate what they said. Rather, when God places life in it and its nature, death and its nature are removed. And this green tree has a nature of moisture and coolness, yet from it comes forth fire, hot and dry. Then He mentioned what is clearer to minds than any proof: the creation of the heavens and the earth, with their greatness and vastness, and that the weak creation has no comparison to them. And if His power and knowledge were not incapable of this great creation, which is greater than the creation of people, how could He be incapable of giving them life after their death?

Then He established this meaning by mentioning two of His attributes that entail what He informed, so He said: ﴿Yes, indeed, and He is the Creator, the All-Knowing.﴾

His being a Creator and All-Knowing requires that He creates what He wills, and what He wills of creation cannot overpower Him. Then He established this meaning by the fact that the comprehensiveness of His will and its perfection does not fall short concerning it or any thing, ever, so He said: ﴿Indeed, His command, when He intends a thing, is only that He says to it, "Be," and it is.﴾

So it is not possible for it to resist Him, nor is it beyond Him; rather it comes obedient and submissive to His will and intention. Then He added to this emphasis and clarification with His saying: ﴿So exalted is He in whose hand is the dominion of all things.﴾

He thus declared Himself free of what His enemies, the deniers of the Return, had uttered, glorifying Himself by the fact that the dominion of all things is in His hand; He disposes of it with the disposal of the true owner over what he owns, one who cannot be prevented from any disposal he wills concerning it.

Then He concluded the surah with His saying: ﴿And to Him you will be returned.﴾ Just as they began from Him, so their return is to Him; from Him is the beginning and to Him is the return. He is the First and the Last, and ﴿to your Lord is the finality.﴾

(Section)

And he said in: (al-Sawaiq al-Mursalah)

Glorified is He, in establishing the matter of resurrection, saying: ﴿And he presents to Us a parable and forgets his creation. He says, "Who will give life to bones while they are decayed?" Say, "He will give them life who created them the first time, and He is, of every creation, Knowing."﴾ to the end of the surah.

So if the most knowledgeable of people, the most eloquent, and the most capable of expression sought to produce an argument better than this one, or like it, in words resembling these in brevity, conciseness, clarity of indication, and soundness of proof, he would find himself clearly incapable and his hope cut off, and people would be ashamed of him for that.

For He, glorified is He, opened this argument with a question raised by the atheist, which required an answer; and in His saying ﴿and forgets his creation﴾ there was what sufficed as an answer, established the argument, and removed the doubt. Were it not for what He, glorified is He, intended of confirming His argument and increasing its establishment: He informed that this atheist asking about this matter, if he had not forgotten the creation of himself and the beginning of his existence and had remembered his creation, his reflection upon it would have been sufficient for his answer, silencing him from this question. Then He, glorified is He, clarified what His saying ﴿and forgets his creation﴾ included, and stated it explicitly as an answer to his question, so He said: ﴿Say: He will give them life who created them the first time﴾ [Ya-Sin: 79].

So He argued from the originating to the restoring, and from the first creation to the other creation, since every rational person knows by necessary knowledge that whoever is able to do this is able to do that; and that if He were incapable of the second, He would be even more incapable of the first. And since creation entails the Creator's power over His creation and His knowledge of its details, He followed that with His saying: ﴿And He is, of every creation, Knowing﴾.

So He is knowing of the first creation, its details, its particulars, its materials, its form, and its four causes.

Likewise He is knowing of the second creation, its details, its materials, and the manner of its production. If He is of complete knowledge and perfect power, how could it be impossible for Him to give life to bones while they are decayed? Then He confirmed the matter with an overpowering proof and a manifest demonstration that includes an answer to another atheist's question, who says: when bones become decayed, their nature returns to cold and dry, and life must have as its matter and bearer a nature that is hot and moist in order to receive the form of life. So He, glorified is He, undertook the answer to this question with what indicates the matter of resurrection; in it is both the proof and the answer together. So He said: ﴿He who produces for you fire from the green tree, and then you ignite from it﴾ [Ya-Sin: 80]. Thus He informed of bringing forth this element, which is in the extreme of heat and dryness, from the green tree full of moisture and coolness. So He who brings a thing out of its opposite, and to whom the materials and elements of created things are subject and do not resist Him, is the One who does what the atheist denied and rejected: giving life to bones while they are decayed. Then He emphasized this by deriving the proof from the greater, most magnificent thing to the easier, smaller thing, and that every rational person knows that whoever is able over the great and glorious is far more able over what is less than it, and more and more able.

So whoever is able to carry a qintar (a great weight) is far more mighty in carrying an ounce. So He said: ﴿Is not He who created the heavens and the earth able to create the like of them?﴾

So He informed that He who originated the heavens and the earth, with their majesty, the greatness of their affair, the size of their bodies, their vastness, and the wonder of their creation, is more able to give life to bones that have become decayed, returning them to their former state, as He said in another place: ﴿The creation of the heavens and the earth is greater than the creation of people, but most people do not know﴾ [Ghafir: 57].

And He said: ﴿Do they not see that Allah, who created the heavens and the earth and was not wearied by their creation, is able to give life to the dead? Yes, indeed; He is over all things competent﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 33].

Then, glorified is He, took this and explained it with another explanation that includes, along with establishing the argument, the removal of the doubt of every atheist and denier: that His act is not like the act of others, who act by tools, with effort, fatigue, and hardship, and cannot independently accomplish the act but must have with them a tool, a partner, and a helper. Rather, in creating what He wills to create, the mere act of His will suffices, and His saying to the thing to be brought into being, "Be," so it is, as He wills and intends.

So He informed of the execution of His will and intention, the swiftness of His bringing into being, and the obedience of what is brought into being to Him, and that it does not resist Him.

Then He concluded this argument by informing that the dominion of all things is in His hand, so that He disposes of it by His action; and that is His saying: ﴿And to Him you will be returned﴾ [Ya-Sin: 83].

Blessed is He who spoke these words, which gathered within themselves, in their brevity, clarity, eloquence, and soundness of proof, everything for which there is need: the establishment of the proof, the answer to the doubt, the refutation of the atheist's argument, and the silencing of the obstinate, in words none sweeter to the ear, none sweeter in their meanings to the heart, and none more beneficial in their fruit for the servant.

[Section: Selling the Bone of a Carcass]

As for its bone: whoever does not render it impure by death, such as Abu Hanifa, some of the companions of Ahmad, and the opinion chosen by Ibn Wahb from among the companions of Malik, holds that its sale is permissible according to them, even though the basis of purity differs. The companions of Abu Hanifa said: it does not enter into "carrion" and its name does not apply to it, and they denied that pain is evidence of its being alive. They said: it is only the flesh adjacent to it that causes it pain, not the bone itself. They interpreted His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Who will give life to bones while they are decayed?﴾ [Ya-Sin: 78] as involving the omission of a noun, meaning "the owners of the bones." Others weakened this basis greatly and said: the bone feels pain sensibly, and its pain is more intense than the pain of flesh; and it is not sound to interpret the verse as involving omission of a noun, for two reasons. The first: it is positing something for which there is no evidence, so there is no path to it. The second: this assumption entails turning away from answering the questioner's query who found it problematic that bones could live. For Ubayy ibn Khalaf took a decayed bone, then came with it to the Prophet ﷺ, crumbled it in his hand, and said: "O Muhammad! Do you think Allah will give life to this after it has decayed?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Yes, and He will resurrect you, and cause you to enter the Fire."

So the basis of purity is that the cause of the impurity of carrion is absent in bones, so they are not judged impure, and it is not sound to analogize them to flesh; because the retention of moisture and the foul waste is specific to flesh and not to bones, just as what has no flowing blood does not become impure by death, and it is a complete animal, due to the absence of the cause of impurity in it. Bone is more deserving of this, and this basis is sounder and stronger than the first. On this basis, the sale of the bones of carrion is permissible when they come from an animal whose substance is pure.

As for whoever sees their impurity, it is not permissible to sell them, since their impurity is intrinsic. Ibn al-Qasim said: Malik said: I do not think the bones of carrion should be bought or sold, nor elephant tusks, nor should they be traded in, nor should one comb with their combs, nor oil oneself with their oil-vessels. How can oil be placed in carrion, or one comb his beard with bones of carrion while they are wet? He disliked cooking with bones of carrion. Mutarrif and Ibn al-Majishun permitted the sale of elephant tusks without qualification. Ibn Wahb and Asbagh permitted it if they are boiled and scalded, and they considered that a tanning of them.
